items.title: Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: I said an old drummer, he taught me that his name was Cantrell. He said when you tighten your drum up, don't let it down.

ctx.x: Makes it sound like a heavy rhythm.

It really sounded like a brass band. They had an awful good band, but it sounded to me like a young brass band. Yeah, it didn't swing and that light drive. No, no, we played, O'er used to play even the blues, see, when he played that four beats. We used to call it rockin' time. Yeah, rockin' time. That's right. Because he always said he'd make people pass their foot, that's what we'd get it. But no, that's two beats, that just started years, you know, late years, people moth and that same, but we played four…
See. How thick a shell do you use? A five or six inch or how big is it? Do you know? Is it a fairly deep one or is it shallow?
